page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The processor includes a 38 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES. The system is equipped with 85.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.08 GB per core. It integrates a single NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPU with 40 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU performance is weak, as evidenced by lower scores in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the average tier. However, the server excels in machine learning workloads. LLM inference speeds for prompt processing and text generation using small (135M) and medium (7B) models rank in the top tier, demonstrating the high efficiency of the onboard NVIDIA A100 GPU. Conversely, prompt processing for large (70B) models drops to average performance due to the memory constraints of a single GPU.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a specialized hardware profile where the primary value resides in the GPU accelerator rather than general-purpose compute power. Utilizing this instance for standard CPU-bound tasks or basic web serving results in resource underutilization. It is highly optimized for workloads that can offload computation to the GPU, such as deep learning training, medium-scale LLM inference, data science pipelines, and parallelized scientific simulations.
